roads.name: Chūma road
roads.japanese: 中馬街道 (三州街道 / 伊那街道)
roads.note: Okazaki up the Tomoe and Asuke valleys, over the Inabu uplands (Neba, Hiraya, Namiai) to Iida, then north up the Ina valley to Shiojiri; the pack-horse (chūma) salt and goods road from the Mikawa coast into Shinano.
roads.source: ja.wikipedia 飯田街道 / 三州街道 (Sanshū or Chūma kaidō, one of the Nagoya/Okazaki-Iida roads mapped 1701-1840); the Chūma carriers' rights were confirmed by the shogunate in 1764, but they had worked the road since the 1600s; Iijima jin'ya on it from 1677.

roads.name: Akiba road
roads.note: Kakegawa - Mori - Inui to the Akiha fire-god shrine, then north along the Median Tectonic Line: Misakubo, Aokuzure pass, Tōyama (Wada, Kamimura), Ōshika, Bunkui pass, Takatō, Tsuetsuki pass to Suwa (Chino). An old salt road turned pilgrim road.
roads.source: ja.wikipedia 秋葉街道 (Kakegawa - Mori - Ichinose - Inui - Sakashita - Akiha-san; earlier a salt road, Edo-period Akiha pilgrimage); pass positions from GSI.

roads.name: Suruga road
roads.japanese: 駿州往還 (河内路 / 身延道)
roads.note: Okitsu on the Tōkaidō up the Fuji River gorge through Manzawa, Nanbu, Minobu, Shimoyama and Iwama to Kajikazawa, then across the basin to Kōfu. The Minobu pilgrims' road; the river beside it carried boats from 1607.
roads.source: ja.wikipedia 駿州往還 (Kawauchi-ji / Minobu-michi, Kōfu - Okitsu, relay stations Iwama, Shimoyama, Nanbu, Manzawa listed under the Anayama; Sengoku-era road kept in the Edo period).

roads.name: Kamakura road
roads.note: Kōfu - Isawa - Kurokoma - Misaka pass - Kawaguchi - Yoshida - Lake Yamanaka - Kagosaka pass - Subashiri - Gotemba; beyond Gotemba it crossed the Ashigara pass (shared with the Yagurazawa road). The Fuji-pilgrim and Kai-to-Sagami road.
roads.source: MLIT Kantō 'Misaka / Kamakura-ōkan' page and Agency for Cultural Affairs 'Rekishi no michi 100' (1996); post-horse stations at Isawa, Kawaguchi and near Kagosaka; oldest recorded Kai road (Engi-shiki).

roads.name: Yagurazawa road
roads.note: Edo (Akasaka gate) - Sangenjaya - Futako ferry - Nagatsuta - Atsugi - Isehara (for Ōyama) - Hadano - Matsuda - Sekimoto - Yagurazawa checkpoint - Ashigara pass - Gotemba - Numazu. The Ōyama pilgrims' road and the Tōkaidō's back door.
roads.source: ja.wikipedia 矢倉沢往還 (Akasaka-mon to Numazu via Ashigara pass, a waki-ōkan of the Tōkaidō; called Ōyama kaidō from the mid-Edo pilgrim boom).

roads.name: Nakahara road
roads.note: Edo (Toranomon) - Maruko ferry - Kosugi - Saedo - Seya - Yoda - Sagami River - Nakahara (Hiratsuka): a straight inland short-cut used by carters and merchants dodging the Tōkaidō.
roads.source: ja.wikipedia 中原街道 (so named after the shogunate's 1604 works; relay points Kosugi, Saedo, Seya, Yoda).

roads.name: Shimo-kaidō
roads.note: Nagoya - Kachigawa - Sakashita - Utsu pass - Ikeda - Tajimi - Takayama - Toki - Kamado - Makigane fork on the Nakasendō near Ōi: the busy 'back road' from Nagoya to the Kiso road and Zenkō-ji.
roads.source: ja.wikipedia 下街道 (善光寺道): side road of the Nakasendō, stages listed in the 1765 Tōkai Kiso ryōdōchū; unofficial (no licensed stations) but in use through the Edo period.

roads.name: Kami-kaidō
roads.note: Nagoya - Kusunoki - Komaki - Gakuden - Haguro - Zenshiji - Fushimi on the Nakasendō: the Owari domain's official road to the Kiso valley.
roads.source: ja.wikipedia 上街道 (木曽街道): Owari domain road, Komaki post laid out 1623-1628, joins the Nakasendō at Fushimi-juku.

roads.name: Yamato road
roads.japanese: 大和街道 (加太越奈良道)
roads.note: Seki on the Tōkaidō - Kabuto pass - Tsuge - Sanago - Iga Ueno - Shimagahara - Kasagi - Kamo - Kizu - Nara: the Iga road, a short-cut from the Tōkaidō to Nara and on to Osaka.
roads.source: Mie Prefecture 'Mie no rekishi kaidō: Yamato kaidō' (bunka.pref.mie.lg.jp); Edo name Kabuto-goe Nara-michi; ex-Tōkaidō of the Nara period.

roads.name: Kuragari road
roads.note: Osaka (Tamatsukuri) east across the Kawachi plain to Hiraoka, over the steep Kuragari pass in the Ikoma hills and down to Nara: the shortest Osaka-Nara road, busy with Ise pilgrims.
roads.source: ja.wikipedia 暗越奈良街道 (Nara-period origin; Edo-period secondary road with inns, daimyō and Ise-pilgrim traffic).

roads.name: Godaisan road
roads.note: Tsuchiyama on the Tōkaidō north through Kamagake, Ishihara (Hino), Okamoto, Yōkaichi and Obata to the Nakasendō near Echigawa: a true cross-road between the two highways, used by the court's proxy pilgrims to Ise and Taga.
roads.source: ja.wikipedia 御代参街道 (opened 1640 for Kasuga-no-Tsubone's Ise-to-Taga pilgrimage; the name itself is only attested late, 1868).

roads.name: Saku road
roads.japanese: 佐久甲州街道 (佐久往還)
roads.note: Nirasaki on the Kōshū road - Wakamiko - Nagasawa - Hirasawa pass (Nobeyama) - Umi-no-kuchi - down the Chikuma River via Takanomachi and Nozawa to Iwamurada on the Nakasendō: joins the Kōshū road to the Nakasendō behind Yatsugatake.
roads.source: sakucci.or.jp 'Saku rekishi no michi: Saku-Kōshū-dō' (Nirasaki - Iwamurada, about 18 ri; relay villages Nakajō, Wakamiko, Nagasawa, Hirasawa, Umi-no-kuchi, Umijiri, Kaminohata, Takanomachi, Nozawa); medieval Zenkō-ji road and Takeda military road.
